title: Integral translates cover a smooth group with connected generic fibre
statement:
Let $D$ be a strictly henselian discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], $F=\operatorname{Frac}D$ and $S=\operatorname{Spec}D$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $M$ be a smooth separated group scheme locally of finite type over $S$ [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; group schemes have multiplication, identity and inverse morphisms satisfying the group diagrams, and separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Suppose $M_F$ is geometrically connected, meaning connected after every extension of $F$ [def-pc-base-change, def-weil-connected-scheme]. Suppose the identity components of the geometric fibres are represented by an open subgroup $Q\subseteq M$ [def-weil-open-immersion]; thus $Q_F=M_F$. For $m\in M(D)$, write $mQ$ for the image of $Q$ under left multiplication by $m$. Then
$$M=\bigcup_{m\in M(D)}mQ$$
as an open covering. Consequently, for every local homomorphism $D\to C$ to a nonzero commutative local ring, every $z\in M(C)$ has an expression $z=m_Cu$ with $m\in M(D)$ and $u\in Q(C)$. Here points mean sections of the respective group schemes and $m_C$ denotes base change of the section $m$. No finite-type or Néron mapping property of $M$ is assumed beyond the stated local finite type.

source.place: Agent-extracted component input to BLR 10.1 Proposition 7, printed pp.292–293 (PDF pp.298–299); ingredients read locally in Stacks varieties.tex Tag 056U (lemma-smooth-separable-closed-points-dense) and more-algebra.tex Tag 0H74 (lemma-lift-smooth-henselian). Primary scan https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf; local BLR PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Put $k=D/\mathfrak m$ and $G=M_k$. Strict henselianity says that $k$ is separably closed and $(D,\mathfrak m)$ is henselian. Smooth base change makes $G/k$ smooth. It is locally of finite type: on affine charts, base changing finitely many algebra generators of a locally finite-type chart of $M/S$ still gives finitely many generators. A field is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0$ and the unit ideal), so $G$ is locally Noetherian by pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft. Each affine open $W$ has Noetherian coordinate ring by pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth, hence Noetherian underlying space by lem-sc-affine-noetherian-underlying-space. Its connected components are open by lem-sfb-noetherian-connected-components-open. For $x\in G$, the connected component of $x$ in any affine open neighbourhood $W$ is therefore an open neighbourhood of $x$ in $G$ contained in the connected component of $x$ in $G$. Thus every connected component of $G$ is open. Give each such component its open-subscheme structure.

source.place: Tags 04MF (lemma-locally-Noetherian-locally-connected) and 04ME (lemma-locally-connected), affine-neighbourhood argument; smooth base change: morphisms.tex Tag 01VB; local Noetherianity: Tag 01T6

proof.text: Let $\bar k/k$ be an algebraic closure and $C_e$ the connected component of the identity in $G$, now an open $k$-subscheme. The projection $X_{\bar k}\to X$ is surjective for every $k$-scheme $X$: apply lem-pc-field-extension-surjective and lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change. In particular $Q_k$ is connected, since $(Q_k)_{\bar k}=Q_{\bar k}$ is the assumed geometric identity component and its continuous image is all of $Q_k$. It contains the identity, so $Q_k\subseteq C_e$. Conversely $C_e$ is geometrically connected by lem-weil-separably-closed-geometrically-connected. Its base change is connected and contains the identity, so $(C_e)_{\bar k}\subseteq Q_{\bar k}$. Surjectivity of $(C_e)_{\bar k}\to C_e$ implies $C_e\subseteq Q_k$. Consequently $Q_k=C_e$ as open subschemes of $G$: both structure sheaves are restrictions of $\mathcal O_G$ to the same open set.

source.place: Tag 0363 (lemma-separably-closed-field-connected-components), geometric connectedness over a separably closed field; Tag 01S1 (morphisms-lemma-base-change-surjective)

proof.text: For any connected component $C$ of $G$, its open subscheme is smooth over $k$ by lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes. It is nonempty by the definition of a component. By lem-pc-dense-separable-points it has a closed point $a$ with $\kappa(a)/k$ finite separable. Because $k$ is separably closed, this extension is $k$ itself; hence $a$ determines a $k$-point of $C$, and thus of $G$. This applies to every component, with no finiteness assumption on the collection of components.

source.place: Tag 056U (lemma-smooth-separable-closed-points-dense), applied to the nonempty smooth open component C

proof.text: Choose an affine open neighbourhood $V=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq M$ of the image of $a:\operatorname{Spec}k\to M$. The point factors through $V$ by lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme. Restriction to $V$ is smooth over $S=\operatorname{Spec}D$ by lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes, so $B$ is a smooth $D$-algebra by lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine. The point corresponds to a $D$-algebra map $B\to k=D/\mathfrak m$. Apply lem-trf-henselian-smooth-algebra-lifting with $R=A=D$, its smooth algebra $B$, and $I=\mathfrak m$. It gives a $D$-algebra map $B\to D$ reducing to the prescribed point. Taking spectra and composing with $V\hookrightarrow M$ gives $m\in M(D)$ with $m_k=a$. Thus every component C has such a lifted point.

source.place: Tag 0H74 (lemma-lift-smooth-henselian); affine smoothness and restriction: morphisms.tex Tag 01V6 (lemma-smooth-characterize)

proof.text: Left multiplication by any section $m$ is an $S$-isomorphism of $M$ with inverse left multiplication by $m^{-1}$, by the group diagrams. It therefore sends the open subscheme $Q$ to an open subscheme $mQ$. For the lifted point of a component $C$ in step 4, its special-fibre map is left multiplication by $a$. A homeomorphism takes a maximal connected subset to the maximal connected subset of its image point (apply the inverse homeomorphism for maximality). Thus it takes $C_e$ onto $C$, because it takes the identity to $a$. Step 2 gives $(mQ)_k=aQ_k=C$. Since the components partition $G$ and the projection $G=M_k\to M$ is a homeomorphism onto the set-theoretic fibre over the closed point [def-pc-scheme-fibre], the union of all the $mQ$ contains every point of $M$ over $\mathfrak m$. It also contains every point of $M$ over $(0)$: take the identity section, use $Q_F=M_F$ and the same fibre homeomorphism for $M_F\to M$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. A DVR has only the primes $(0)$ and $\mathfrak m$: a nonzero prime contains a nonzero element, which is a unit times a power of a uniformizer by lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power (a DVR is a principal ideal domain, hence Noetherian, with maximal ideal generated by a nonzero uniformizer), hence contains the uniformizer and equals $\mathfrak m$. Every point of $M$ lies over one of these primes. The open subschemes $mQ$ therefore cover $M$.

source.place: Connected components and homeomorphisms; elementary group-diagram translation argument, using the assumed open subgroup and equality Q_F=M_F

proof.text: Let $D\to C$ be the stated local map and let $c$ be the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}C$ (it exists since $C\ne0$). Choose $m\in M(D)$ with $z(c)\in mQ$ using the open cover just proved. Then $z^{-1}(mQ)$ is an open subset of $\operatorname{Spec}C$ containing $c$, and is all of $\operatorname{Spec}C$: a basic neighbourhood $D(f)$ of the maximal ideal has $f$ outside that ideal, hence $f$ a unit and $D(f)=\operatorname{Spec}C$. By lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme, $z$ factors through $mQ$. Composing this factorization with the inverse translation gives $u\in Q(C)$. The group identity for the translation and its inverse yields $z=m_Cu$, as required.

source.place: Open-subscheme factorization; elementary local-spectrum basic-open argument and group identities
